summary: A is closer to the contract and substantially more reviewable, though it still needs correction before merge. B introduces a broad RawClient retry/ownership change and duplicates Files.Add logic, directly conflicting with the frozen scope.
reasons: A reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile and centralizes request construction, option handling, decoding, and errors in one private add path shared by Add and Upload.
A’s tests directly verify multipart field name, filename, content, and replay of an upload sourced from os.File after a 429.
B duplicates Files.Add’s request and response implementation inside Upload instead of routing through Add, creating maintenance and semantic-drift risk.

B changes global RawClient behavior for every io.ReadSeeker, including retry eligibility, content length, seeking, and reader ownership. The contract explicitly excludes refactoring unrelated retry machinery and requires FilesOption/Add behavior to remain unchanged.
risks_a: A changes existing Add behavior by eagerly reading and buffering every caller-provided multipart body, affecting streaming, memory use, and when reader errors occur.
Upload calls the new private add helper rather than the existing FilesService.Add method, contrary to the contract’s explicit routing requirement.
The visible tests do not cover Upload validation or source-reader failures.
risks_b: Upload bypasses FilesService.Add and copies its option, request, decoding, and missing-data logic.
The RawClient change expands scope and alters existing APIs beyond the requested convenience upload path.
